title: Latency drilldown journey mapping — sketches & notes
content:
Context:
This doc captures early exploration for a latency-focused trace viewer flow aimed at faster root-cause discovery for product engineers and SREs. The idea is to combine a compact waterfall with a timeline heatmap and persistent annotations/anchors so users can traverse long traces quickly and land on the most suspicious regions.

Goals:
- Surface latency hotspots across a trace at-a-glance (heatmap overview).
- Allow keyboard-forward, low-visual-noise navigation for power users and support investigators who debug many traces per day.
- Enable lightweight annotations (user notes, suspect-span flags) that persist to trace metadata and can be shared with teammates.
- Minimize vertical scrolling for traces with large numbers of spans while enabling fast contextual drilldown.

Primary personas:
- Platform SRE (Jane): needs to triage production incidents quickly, often with noisy traces.
- Backend engineer (Marco): investigates service-to-service latency regressions and wants to correlate trace hotspots with deploys and metrics.
- Observability product manager (Ayesha): wants to prototype and test new interactions with users.

High-level interaction sketches (verbal):
1) Top: compact heatmap timeline (mini-rail) spanning trace duration. Each pixel column represents a small bucket (e.g., 50ms); color intensity maps aggregated latency or error-rate. Hover reveals mini-hover tooltip with top-2 contributing spans.
2) Below heatmap: condensed waterfall with one-line span rows (left: service + op, right: relative bar showing start/end). Spans grouped by service by default; toggle to "expand thread" to show child spans inline.
3) Sticky annotation bar (right rail): shows open annotations for the selected time window or selected span. Annotations are small chips with author and timestamp; clicking an annotation jumps/zooms the heatmap and waterfall to the anchored window.
4) Keyboard navigation: J/K to move hotspot to previous/next heatmap bucket; Enter to open span detail; A to add annotation at current bucket; / to quick-search span names or attributes; ? shows cheat sheet overlay.
5) Mini trace breadcrumbs above waterfall: timeline pins for deploys, config changes, or external events (sourced from linked artifacts). Pins are tappable and center the view to the nearest bucket.

Detailed behaviors and edge cases:
- Very long traces: heatmap should be interactive; users can lasso-drag to select a range which zooms the waterfall to that window. When zoomed, span rows switch from one-line compact to full waterfall with KV list on the right.
- Mixed durations: use a logarithmic color scale to avoid short spikes washing out long-but-not-dominant spans. Provide a toggle "linear/log" in the heatmap legend.
- Sampling / missing spans: when spans are missing for a bucket, show a faint hatch and an explanation tooltip ("span sampling: 40% for this service").
- Annotation conflicts: if two users annotate the same time window, show stacked chips and allow toggling a threaded view.

Acceptance criteria for an initial MVP (engineering):
- Heatmap overview + single-click zoom to time window implemented (supports traces up to 1000 spans).
- One-line collapsed waterfall with grouping by service and expand toggle.
- Add/Edit/Delete annotations persisted to trace metadata (simple API available in trace service).
- Keyboard shortcuts: J/K/Enter/A// implemented and documented in cheat sheet.
- Basic unit/integration tests for navigation and annotation APIs.

Backlog / next steps (roughly prioritized):
- P0: Persist annotations and link to ticket system (JIRA-ORT-89). Add test coverage for heatmap mapping logic.
- P1: Add lasso selection for heatmap and animated zoom transition. Create UX benchmarks: median time-to-first-hotspot-click.
- P2: Add correlation overlay with deploy pins and metric-sparkline mini-charts.
- P3: User-configurable bucket size and color scale presets.
- P4: Export annotated views as short URLs and snapshots for postmortems.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Annotation model: free text + tags vs structured categories (suspect-service, external-call, cache-miss). Recommendation: MVP = free text + optional tag list.
- Persistence: should annotations be editable by anyone on the team or only author+admins? Ops usually want editable comments; security team may prefer stricter controls. Proposal: default editable by author and workspace admins.
- Telemetry: what metrics do we capture for heatmap interactions (clicks, lasso selects, zooms)? Need to define event taxonomy for analytics.

Design notes / tiny wireframes (text sketches):
- [heatmap rail] ----|=================^^^====|----  (color intensity bars)
- Breadcrumbs: [deploy@09:03] [config-change@09:07] [autoscale@09:10]
- Waterfall: serviceA:handler             |----|        
            serviceB:db-query            |---|          
            serviceA:cache-get           -|             (bars scaled to zoom window)
- Right rail annotations: [chip: "suspect db index" - Priya 11/9] [chip: "retry storm" - Marco 11/9]

Prototype tasks for next sprint (engineer + designer pairing):
- Low-fi prototype: clickable Figma frames showing heatmap + keyboard nav. (Owner: Ayesha)
- Wireframe to component mapping: list required states for Heatmap, CollapsedWaterfallRow, AnnotationChip, CheatSheet. (Owner: Marco)
- Backend: small annotations API + DB table mapping (owner: infra/observability).

Notes on adoption and rollout strategy:
- Feature flag behind "trace-latency-drilldown" on dev and beta orgs.
- Roll to 5% of hosted accounts with heavy trace volume, collect time-to-first-insight metrics.
- Run 3 short user interviews with SREs to validate keyboard flow vs mouse-first expectations.

References / inspiration:
- Existing trace viewers (span aggregation + timeline) + ideas from APM heatmaps (Datadog timeline heatmap), but optimized for keyboard-first and persistent annotations.
- Linked artifact: JIRA-ORT-89 contains basic API contract for annotation persistence.

Quick grooming notes (for backlog refinement meeting):
- Split heatmap into front-end visual layer (rendering + bucket math) and backend rollup endpoint that returns color intensity per bucket.
- Decide on default bucket width: start with 50ms for traces < 30s, scale up to 250ms for traces > 5m.
- UX should expose a "normalize by service" toggle that computes heatmap based on per-service percentile rather than absolute ms (helps multi-service traces).

End of notes.
